title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 67-69): Grothendieck is setting up 'cartes triangulaires pondérées', i.e. dessins d'enfants, as finite sets with an action of the oriented triangle group Π_{0,3} = <ρ_0, ρ_1, ρ_∞ | ρ_0ρ_1ρ_∞ = 1>, or of its extension Π_{0,3}^τ by complex conjugation in the non-oriented case. Equivalently these are finite covers of P^1_C branched over {0,1,∞}. On this page he discusses imposing relations ρ_i^{ν_i} = 1 (eq. 29). Such a relation means that every vertex of type i (a point over i) has order, i.e. valency or ramification index, dividing ν_i.

He then specializes to ordinary maps (cartes ordinaires). Via barycentric subdivision these are the triangulated maps with ρ_1^2 = 1: type-0 points are the vertices, type-1 points are the edge midpoints, type-∞ points are the face centres. Then (30) ρ_0^{ν_0} = 1 (resp. ρ_∞^{ν_∞} = 1) says the vertex valencies (resp. face degrees) divide ν_0 (resp. ν_∞).

For (31) ρ_1^{ν_1} = 1 there are two cases, since ρ_1^2 = 1 already holds:
- ν_1 even: the relation is automatic.
- ν_1 odd: the relation forces ρ_1 = 1. The cover is then unramified over 1, hence branched only over 0 and ∞. Since π_1(C^*) = Z, a connected such cover is the cyclotomic cover z ↦ z^n.

The corresponding map is the regular spherical map with automorphism group Z/nZ ≅ μ_n(C). It has one vertex (at 0), one face (around ∞), and n edges arranged circularly. These are really n dangling semi-edges ending at the n-th roots of unity, i.e. fixed points of ρ_1. The marginal sketch shows a sphere with a pole and n half-arcs hanging from it. Grothendieck calls this case 'relativement trivial'.

The next page completes the thread. Allowing ν_i ∈ N* ∪ {∞}, the maps satisfying the conditions are the finite sets acting through Π_{0,3}/<ρ_i^{ν_i}>. These are the (generalized) triangle groups, identified with orbifold fundamental groups ('groupe fondamental avec signature', fundamental group of the multiplicity) of P^1 with signature ν_0 R_0 + ν_1 R_1 + ν_∞ R_∞. The purpose is to organize dessins with bounded ramification and to relate them to triangle groups and orbifold uniformization.
errors: No mathematical error. The z^n case implicitly needs maps that allow fixed points of ρ_1 (free semi-edges). Under the stricter convention of maps without semi-edges (ρ_1 fixed-point free), ν_1 odd simply gives no nonempty maps. Grothendieck's reading is the correct one for his framework, where ρ_1^2 = 1 only.
Minor: the equation number (31) is reused on the next page for a different statement, a numbering slip in the manuscript.

ideas.what: Imposing ρ_i^{ν_i} = 1 on dessins / triangulated maps bounds the ramification orders over 0, 1, ∞; such maps correspond to actions of the quotient triangle group
ideas.modern_name: Dessins/maps of type (ν_0, ν_1, ν_∞); actions of (generalized) triangle groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Jones–Singerman (1978), building on classical work on regular maps (Coxeter–Moser, Brahana); Grothendieck (Esquisse d'un programme, 1984)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (section on cartes and triangle groups / multiplicities)

ideas.what: Ordinary maps as triangulated maps with ρ_1^2 = 1 via barycentric subdivision; vertex valencies and face degrees governed by ρ_0 and ρ_∞
ideas.modern_name: Maps as permutation representations of the cartographic group C_2 = <ρ_0, ρ_1 | ρ_1^2 = 1>

ideas.what: Odd ν_1 with ρ_1^2 = 1 forces ρ_1 = 1, so the cover is branched only over 0 and ∞, i.e. the cyclotomic cover z ↦ z^n; the associated regular spherical map has one vertex, one face and n semi-edges, with group μ_n
ideas.modern_name: Star dessin of z^n (degenerate regular map with semi-edges)

ideas.what: Quotients of Π_{0,3} as orbifold fundamental groups with signature (developed on the next page)
ideas.modern_name: Orbifold fundamental group of P^1 with cone points; triangle groups
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme ('multiplicités', groupes fondamentaux avec signature)

deep.surprise_reason: A routine expository passage of the dessins d'enfants / triangle group framework already present in Esquisse d'un programme and in Jones–Singerman. The only detail is the explicit treatment of the degenerate odd-ν_1 case (z^n), which is elementary.
transcription_corrections: Top-left margin carries the archive folio number '68'; the '10' at top centre is Grothendieck's own page number.
'la carte [-correspond-] à un' reads in the image as 'la carte correspondant à un', with 'correspondant' partly struck out.
'(resp. que les faces ont d'ordre divisant ν∞)' should read '(resp. que les faces sont d'ordre divisant ν∞)'.
'sphériques' is a marginal insertion in the left margin next to 'de groupe Z/nZ'.

'(carte isomorphe : n demi-[?] cercles, visiblement)' is uncertain. The word after 'demi-' is unclear in the image ('demi-droites' / 'demi-arcs' are plausible); the sketch shows n half-arcs from a pole on a sphere.
'(n∈N)' sits at the start of the following line, before the struck-out 'cas que' and the inserted 'donnant lieu'.
